About The Role

Intake Specialist

The Intake Specialist plays a vital role in supporting patient access to care by coordinating referrals, reviewing clinical documentation, and ensuring services are set up accurately and efficiently. You’ll work closely with patients, providers, referral sources, and internal teams to navigate insurance requirements, confirm eligibility, and move the intake process forward smoothly.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys detail-oriented work, patient communication, and collaborating across teams in a fast-paced healthcare environment. This is an early in career position and the hourly compensation range reflects this. Also, must be willing to work on Eastern or Central Standard/Daylight Time.

Core Responsibilities

Review medical records, clinical documentation, and payer guidelines to determine patient eligibility, qualification status, and compliance prior to service delivery
Communicate with patients regarding financial responsibility, collect payments when applicable, and document interactions accurately
Contact patients when documentation does not meet payer requirements, providing updates and alternative options to support timely care
Work with referral sources, physicians, and clinical teams to obtain complete and compliant documentation
Demonstrate expert knowledge of payer requirements to ensure services are provided appropriately and in compliance
Maintain accurate, timely documentation of patient information and communications using electronic systems
Accurately enter referrals within established timeframes while meeting productivity and quality standards
Coordinate with leadership to ensure appropriate inventory and services are selected and scheduled
Work closely with sales, insurance verification, and internal support teams to facilitate the referral and intake process
Navigate multiple EMR and online systems to obtain and manage documentation.
Ensure appropriate shipping and delivery methods are selected in accordance with company procedures
Answer incoming calls promptly and provide professional assistance to patients and referral sources
Participate in on-call rotation during non-business hours in accordance with company policy
Support team operations and quality standards by following company policies and procedures
Performs other related duties as assigned

Experience in management, administrative, clerical, insurance, billing, claims, call center, or customer service preferred but not required
Experience within a healthcare organization, pharmacy, HME, medical supply, or Medicare-certified environment is a plus but not required
Excellent verbal and written communication skills including analytical, problem-solving and decision-making abilities with attention to detail
Ability to multi-task in a fast paced environment
Proficient computer skills – Microsoft Office and healthcare systems are a plus
Comfort learning new technologies and navigating multiple systems
Ability to work independently while following established procedures and directives

What You’ll Do

The Behavioral Health Specialist (BHS) plays a vital, hands-on role in shaping the daily experience of adolescent and young adult patients in Newport Healthcare’s behavioral health programs. As a frontline team member, you’ll create a safe, structured, and compassionate environment where patients feel supported, seen, and empowered throughout their healing journey.

Responsibilities

This role isn’t just important; it’s foundational. BHS team members are the heart of our care model, offering meaningful connection and stability that make a lasting difference in young people’s lives. Key responsibilities include:

Creating a safe and supportive space by offering consistent, compassionate care and supervision that ensures patients’ emotional and physical well-being
Guiding and encouraging patients as they move through their daily schedule—including therapy, group activities, meals, and moments of transition in between
Leading or supporting experiential activities (such as mindfulness practices, recreation, and group experiences) that promote healing and connection
Modeling calm, respectful behavior and healthy coping strategies in a way that builds trust and emotional safety

Collaborating and communicating with team members to support a connected, unified care environment

A patient-first mindset that inspires you to reach the highest standards in supporting the young people in your care
Flexibility within a fast-paced, changing environment—schedules may include day, evening, overnight, weekend, or holiday shifts, and you may need to respond to urgent or unexpected conditions during your shift
Ability to remain calm and composed, and to make good decisions using a combination of analysis, wisdom, experience, and judgment
The capacity to listen attentively and actively, with patience, empathy, and cultural sensitivity
A collaborative team player who can find common ground, build trust with colleagues, and communicate effectively
A problem-solver who digs deep and uses all the information available to craft skillful solutions
Must be at least 21 years old, with a valid driver’s license
High school diploma or GED required; bachelor’s in psychology, counseling, or sociology preferred

Compensation for this role ranges from $20-$24 per hour depending on education and experience.

Company Description
Healing Trauma Therapy is a mental health practice dedicated to supporting individuals, families, and communities impacted by trauma. The organization focuses on evidence-informed, compassionate care that promotes resilience, safety, and long-term healing. Team members collaborate to provide accessible services that honor clients’ diverse backgrounds and experiences. Healing Trauma Therapy values professional growth, ethical practice, and a supportive work environment for staff. The practice strives to make a meaningful difference in the Rapid City, SD community through high-quality, trauma-focused services.
Role Description
This is a full-time, on-site Social Worker role based in Rapid City, SD. The Social Worker provides direct client care through assessment, treatment planning, and ongoing individual, family, and group interventions with a strong focus on trauma-informed practice. Day-to-day responsibilities include maintaining accurate and timely documentation, coordinating care with internal and external providers, and advocating for client needs and resources. The role involves facilitating referrals to community services, crisis support when needed, and regular collaboration with the clinical team to review cases and refine treatment plans. The Social Worker also participates in team meetings, professional development activities, and quality improvement initiatives that support best practices in trauma care.
Qualifications

Ability to conduct develop person-centered, trauma-informed treatment plans.
Skills in individual, family, and group counseling, with sensitivity to diverse cultural, socioeconomic, and family backgrounds.
Strong case management abilities, including coordination of services, referrals to community resources, and client advocacy.
Proficiency in maintaining clinical documentation that meets legal, ethical, and organizational standards.
Effective communication and interpersonal skills for working with clients, families, and interdisciplinary teams.
Capacity to manage crises calmly and responsibly, including risk assessments and safety planning when necessary.
Familiarity with trauma-informed care principles, evidence-informed therapeutic approaches, and professional ethics in social work.
Ability to work on-site full time in Rapid City, SD, with reliability, professional boundaries, and respect for confidentiality.
Master’s in Social Work or related field; relevant state licensure or eligibility for licensure preferred.
Prior experience in mental health, trauma services, or community-based social work is beneficial.

Description

Keeping Washington Clean and Evergreen

The Department of Ecology is hiring a Central Region Community Outreach and Environmental Education Specialist 3
within the Water Quality Program .

Location:

Central Region Office in Union Gap, WA .
Upon hire, you must live within a commutable distance from the duty station.

Assignment Pay

This bilingual-designated role requires successful completion of a Spanish language proficiency assessment (verbal and written) as part of the hiring process.
The salary listed includes 5% bilingual assignment pay.

Schedule

This position is eligible for telework and flexible schedule options.
A minimum of one day per week is required in the office.
Schedules are dependent upon position needs and are subject to change.

Application Timeline

Apply by August 25, 2026
Applications submitted after the date above may not be reviewed unless additional qualified applicants are needed.

Duties

You will be the community’s bridge to water quality awareness and action. As the Community Outreach Environmental Education Specialist, you will lead creative, hands-on learning experiences that inspire residents of all ages to become active stewards of their local environment. Through dynamic public engagement, innovative educational programming, and strong partnerships with schools, community groups, and regional partners, you will transform environmental challenges into opportunities for collective impact.

You will design and deliver outreach initiatives that make complex environmental topics accessible, relatable, and locally relevant—whether through interactive workshops, youth programs, public events, or multilingual communications. You will also help build long-term community relationships that support equitable participation and ensure every voice is heard in environmental decision-making.

What You Will Do

Partner with technical experts to craft community-centered engagement strategies that bring water quality science to life and connect residents directly to the mission of protecting the region’s waters.
Serve as a cultural and linguistic bridge by providing Spanish interpretation during workshops, public meetings, school events, and neighborhood canvassing—ensuring every community member can participate fully and confidently.
Spark public learning through accessible outreach—sharing information via presentations, email, web content, and educational materials that help people understand and act on water quality issues.
Translate key outreach materials into Spanish to support inclusive communication and make environmental information easier for more families to access.
Guide thoughtful, on-the-ground engagement efforts—planning, implementing, and evaluating community outreach while elevating community insights and identifying emerging environmental justice needs in the Lower Yakima Valley.
Remove barriers to participation by identifying gaps in access, developing best practices, and creating tailored outreach tools for underserved communities, local interests, governments, industry, and the general public.

Qualifications

For detailed information on how we calculate experience and responses to other frequently asked questions, please visit our Recruitment website .

Required Qualifications

Seven (7) years of experience and/or education related to the duties of the position, which includes the following:

Communication Skills – Ability to share information clearly with diverse audiences to support understanding and informed participation.
Community Engagement – Ability to plan and carry out engagement activities to involve communities in program decisions and actions.
Cultural Humility and Inclusion – Ability to work respectfully with people from diverse cultures and backgrounds to build trust and improve access to agency services.
Outreach and Education Delivery – Ability to develop and deliver accessible outreach materials and learning opportunities to help the public understand program issues and resources.
Bilingual Communication (English/Spanish) – Ability to translate and interpret information accurately to ensure Spanish-speaking communities can fully participate in outreach and engagement activities. This includes: verbal (speaking/listening) and written (reading/writing).
Program and Environmental Knowledge – Ability to understand environmental issues, program activities, and regulatory requirements to share accurate information and support informed public engagement.

Education
involving a major study in environmental, physical, or natural science, education, health sciences, social services, communications or an academic discipline related to the duties of the position.

5 years of experience AND 60-89 semester or 90-134 quarter college credits (Associate’s degree).
4 years of experience AND 90-119 semester or 135-179 quarter college credits.

Must possess and maintain a valid driver's license or provide alternate reliable transportation for travel within the state of Washington.
Must pass the verbal (speaking/listening) and written (reading/writing) Spanish language proficiency tests.

An understanding of environmental justice research, demographic data, and equity focused assessments.
Knowledge and practice of collaborative problem solving, conflict resolution, and participatory planning.
Experience with website and social media content development.

If you are excited about this role and meet the required qualifications, we encourage you to apply. Our Commitment to DEIR

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Respect (DEIR)
are core values central to Ecology's work. We strive to be a workplace where we are esteemed for sharing our authentic identities, while advancing our individual professional goals and collaborating to protect, preserve, and enhance the environment for current and future generations.

Diversity:
We celebrate and appreciate diversity; our unique perspectives and abilities enrich us all and lead to innovative approaches and solutions.

We believe that DEIR is both a goal and an action. We are on a journey, honoring our shared humanity and taking steps to demonstrate our commitment to a vision where each of us is heard, seen, and valued.

Job Description

Job Summary:

Under the general supervision of the Administrative Nurse Manager/Practice Manager, the Practice Supervisor will oversee clinic operations and will have primary responsibility for the supervision of administrative staff at UCSF’s Redwood Shores Specialty Care Clinic (RWS) They will also have shared oversight over patient support staff such as medical assistants, LVNs, etc. in coordination with the Administrative Nurse Manager.

The Practice Supervisor will be responsible for supervising the operational, human resource, administrative and business functions of RWS. These functions include, but are not limited to, practice revenue management, billing systems and procedures, facilities and safety procedures, registration, new patient coordination, scheduling, medical records storage and maintenance, and insurance authorizations. They must have the ability to perform and prioritize multiple tasks and work well with staff, patients and providers. A high degree of independence, initiative, assertiveness, and diplomacy are necessary in dealing with faculty, staff and patients in a complex environment. This role is a working supervisor, and the incumbent will be expected to continue to support practice operations by answering phones, doing registration, scheduling new patients, working on work queues, assisting with basic facilities upkeep, and performing other administrative tasks as assigned. The Practice Supervisor is expected to consistently project a calm, professional and courteous demeanor and is required to comply with the Medical Center House and Telephone Standards and to role model AIDET & Living PRIDE standards at all times.

The Practice Supervisor will work on a regular basis with leadership in the departments of Otolaryngology/Head & Neck Surgery, Orthopaedics, Urology, Audiology, Radiology, and Sterile Processing. This position will also work closely with the practice leadership and providers in supporting practice goals.
